chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn Hamzah al-Adawi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a gate which opens one thousand gates, and each of those gates opens one thousand gates.

key_terms.أَلْفَ بَابٍ: One thousand gates (indicating vastness and multiplicity)
key_terms.بَابًا: A gate (metaphor for a source or category of knowledge)
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'gate of knowledge' taught to Imam Ali by the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith illustrates the concept of *Ilm al-Imam* (the Imam's comprehensive knowledge) by depicting the Prophet’s instruction to Imam Ali as a generative 'gate' that exponentially expands into deeper layers of divine wisdom. This metaphor underscores the Shia belief that the Imams possess an infinite, interconnected reservoir of knowledge derived directly from the Prophet, serving as the living interpretation of the Quran and divine law.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-17 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hamzih al-Adowi, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of Zurarah that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) had said, “God’s Prophet (MGB) taught Ali (MGB) a gate which opens up to one-thousand gates each of which opens up to another thousand gates.”
